newsitem.title: GERMANY: Cartel office settles dispute with Krupp.
newsitem.headline: Cartel office settles dispute with Krupp.

text.p: Germany's cartel office said on Thursday it had settled a long-running dispute with steel group Krupp which had raised regulatory questions over its 1992 merger with Hoesch.

A spokeswoman for the Berlin-based cartel office said the dispute over Fried. Krupp AG Hoesch-Krupp's pledge to sell off parts of Krupp-Brueninghaus AG in order to avoid creating a monopoly in car suspension parts had been settled.

Krupp cancelled the sale pledge at the end of 1993, saying that market conditions had changed. But the company later proposed an alternative which involved selling some operating units to Italy's Rejna SpA.
Following the completion of these transactions, the cartel office found the original pledge to sell the car suspensions operations had been fulfilled, the spokeswoman said.
